story.headline: Lugano go nine clear in Super League
story.summary: Last week's brief had Lugano six points clear; the lead is now nine, and it widened on the very afternoon the chasing pack stumbled
story.display_body: Last week's brief had Lugano six points clear; the lead is now nine, and it widened on the very afternoon the chasing pack stumbled. Young Boys (YB, the Bern club that has dominated the league for years) lost 3–5 at home to FC Zürich, their first defeat of the season after conceding two late goals, and Lugano then beat Basel 2–1 in Ticino for their 11th win in 12 league games. SRF reports it is Lugano's 23rd match without defeat in all competitions, and describes Basel as dominating the ball (about 65 percent) without creating much: their only goal came from Philip Otele in the 37th minute. In the same round, reigning champions Thun beat bottom club Lausanne 5–4 after trailing 1–4 in the 70th minute.
story.why: nine points after 12 rounds is a big cushion, and the two clubs best placed to chase Lugano, YB and Basel, are both struggling right now.

story.headline: Arsenal win at Anfield, go three clear
story.summary: Kai Havertz scored in the first half and Arsenal then defended for their lives: Liverpool did not manage a single shot on target after the break, according to BBC Sport
story.display_body: Kai Havertz scored in the first half and Arsenal then defended for their lives: Liverpool did not manage a single shot on target after the break, according to BBC Sport. It is Arsenal's first Premier League win at Liverpool since 2012, and it came four days after a Carabao Cup (England's second-tier knockout cup) exit at League Two Fleetwood Town, which manager Mikel Arteta said had sharpened his players. The win leaves the reigning champions top with 24 points from nine games, three clear of Manchester City, with Liverpool fifth on 15.
story.why: a three-point lead after nine games is small, but beating a direct rival away from home, with the league's joint-best defence so far (five goals conceded, fewest in the table), is the sort of result title races turn on.

story.headline: Antonelli is youngest F1 world champion
story.summary: Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes driver, clinched the 2026 drivers' title by finishing third behind winner Max Verstappen (Red Bull) and Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari)
story.display_body: Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes driver, clinched the 2026 drivers' title by finishing third behind winner Max Verstappen (Red Bull) and Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari). He is 20 years and 68 days old, beating Sebastian Vettel's record as youngest champion by three years and 66 days, and is the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. He only needed to stay out of trouble: the title could only have gone elsewhere if his team-mate George Russell or Hamilton had won the race. He now leads Verstappen 380 points to 261, with races still to come this season. The race itself, per Autosport, was reshaped by a red flag after Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac hit the wall, which set up a short sprint to the finish that Verstappen held off Hamilton to win — his third victory in four races.
story.why: a driver who was still a teenager until late August has won the sport's biggest prize, and his team-mate Russell is fourth on 250 points.

story.headline: Hamilton wants Ferrari talks after Leclerc clash
story.summary: Hamilton started from pole but lost momentum on lap one when team-mate Charles Leclerc went past by cutting the grass at Turn 5; Verstappen took second
story.display_body: Hamilton started from pole but lost momentum on lap one when team-mate Charles Leclerc went past by cutting the grass at Turn 5; Verstappen took second. Stewards gave Leclerc only a five-second penalty, which Hamilton and Verstappen both called soft, and Hamilton, who said he was "pushed off by my own team-mate", ended up second, short of the win. He said after the race Ferrari "need serious talks". The fight for second in the championship is now tight: Verstappen 261, Hamilton 259, Russell 250 and Leclerc 245.
story.why: Ferrari have two stars and no clear order between them, and with the title gone, the remaining races decide who finishes best of the rest.

story.headline: Yamaha boycotts MotoGP Qatar round
story.summary: Yamaha announced its factory team and its satellite team Pramac will not travel to the Qatar Grand Prix on 6–8 November, citing the ongoing Middle East war and a clause in its employee contracts that lets it bar travel to war-affected regio
story.display_body: Yamaha announced its factory team and its satellite team Pramac will not travel to the Qatar Grand Prix on 6–8 November, citing the ongoing Middle East war and a clause in its employee contracts that lets it bar travel to war-affected regions. Autosport reports at least four riders will miss the race, the season's 20th round. It follows a week of riders pressing MotoGP to cancel or move the event; the same weekend, Marc Marquez won in Malaysia to close in on the title.
story.why: a manufacturer is skipping a race on safety and contract grounds, and Autosport is already asking what it means for Formula 1's Qatar and Abu Dhabi rounds.

story.headline: Vacherot wins Swiss Indoors in Basel
story.summary: Valentin Vacherot of Monaco (ATP 31) came back from a set down to beat Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic (ATP 21) 2–6, 6–3, 6–3
story.display_body: Valentin Vacherot of Monaco (ATP 31) came back from a set down to beat Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic (ATP 21) 2–6, 6–3, 6–3. It is only his second ATP tour title, a little over a year after his surprise win at the Shanghai Masters (a top-tier ATP 1000 event). In the doubles, the Swiss pair Henry Bernet and Dominic Stricker narrowly missed the title. SRF notes Lehecka, who dominated the first set, gave away the decisive break with two unforced errors on his own serve at 3–5.
story.why: Basel is the Swiss tennis calendar's marquee week; there was no Swiss singles finalist, but the doubles final came close.

story.headline: Zverev becomes world number one
story.summary: Alexander Zverev, 29, takes the top ranking for the first time, making him the oldest man to do so in more than 50 years, per BBC Sport
story.display_body: Alexander Zverev, 29, takes the top ranking for the first time, making him the oldest man to do so in more than 50 years, per BBC Sport. It rests on a breakthrough season: he won his first Grand Slams at the French Open (beating Flavio Cobolli in June) and the US Open, and lost the Wimbledon final to Jannik Sinner. BBC notes he has lost 10 straight matches against Sinner, so the ranking does not settle the big rivalries. The BBC piece also records that Zverev has denied past abuse allegations from two former partners; an ATP-commissioned investigation found "insufficient evidence", and a Berlin trial ended after a week with a settlement, not a verdict. Elsewhere, Carlos Alcaraz won the Vienna Open on Sunday 1 November, beating Alex de Minaur 6–1, 6–4.
story.why: the new number one is a two-time major champion this year, but the same report notes Sinner has beaten him ten times running.
